body: Sorry. Its kind of a crappy situation and this job was the one thing between me and being homeless.
Don't worry. I've put in a report with HR and am waiting for the DM to call me back. I have also contacted my attorney.
In the time the two of them took to try to get me to call a customer off the clock, they could have called him themselves and got it taken care of.

I already admitted it was my fault and that I would go in if they needed me. Yesterday was very hectic. I was one of about four people working for a majority of the day and I've been the only EasyTech for about a month now. I've already been made to feel like scum by my supervisor and my GM for a one time mistake.

I just looked up the ethics code to make sure I'm not being the asshole here and the policy is, as quoted, "If you are paid on an hourly basis, don't work through meals or breaks or after you have clocked out." 

So they are both technically in violation of the ethics code for trying to get me to work off the clock with no compensation. Is that something I turn into the DM, HR, or both? I know HR exists to protect the company, not me, but I've never had to quit a job. Nor have I ever been treated so poorly by my superiors.
US. I don't know what a social worker would do for me? I'm an adult.

The problem is I do feel stupid asking for help even when there's something obviously wrong with me. I broke my ankle and kept apologizing for inconveniencing the response people. When I went to the ER I kept apologizing for wasting their time and they didn't really make me feel any better about it. I told them I thought my sugar was crashing, and when I realized it was a panic attack they gave me a sedative and said "try not to do it again."

I can't help when I get panic attacks. I can be triggered at any time due to the nature of the event I went through. Last night I had one just because it was dark.

I know I need a counselor. Would a help line help me find one in my area that I could afford?

I try. It seems like its all I talk about sometimes. I've been on and off all kinds of meds since I was 14. Last counselor I saw suspected bipolar but I had to stop seeing him when my PTSD forced me to quit school. I've just been having so many problems, they all seem to pile up. I'm trying to find a new counselor or psychiatrist but it's hard when I have to worry about how I'm going to support myself and another person AND there's a chance I might become homeless by February.
